# Octopus

A clone of the SR&D Octopus — an 8-way MIDI-controlled switcher — built around a **Teensy 4.1**. Unlike the audio-path loop switchers this generally gets compared to, this version drives 8 **generic relay outputs**: isolated contact closures on ¼" jacks that you patch to whatever you need to switch (amp channel jacks, other pedals' footswitch inputs, etc.), all recalled together as a single "preset" over MIDI, exactly like a footswitch controller flipping a bank on the original unit.

**Status:** schematic and a fully routed 2-layer PCB are done. Both are generated by scripts in `tools/` and verified with `kicad-cli` (ERC, DRC with schematic parity) plus rendered previews. Open `Octopus.kicad_pro` in KiCad to review. Nothing has been fabricated or bench-tested yet.

## Block diagram

```
panel DIN-5 --harness--> J1 --220R--> 6N138 opto (isolated) --> Teensy 4.1 RX1 (3.3 V side)

                                          +--------------------------+
                                          |  Teensy 4.1              |
                                          |  - MIDI parsing          |
                                          |  - preset table (EEPROM) |
                                          |  8x GPIO (pins 2-9)      |----+
                                          +--------------------------+    |
                                                                          v
                                                          +----------------------------+
                                                          | ULN2803A octal darlington  |
                                                          | driver (sinks relay coils) |
                                                          +----------------------------+
                                                            |   |   |  ...  x8
                                                            v   v   v
                                                     8x SPDT relay + status LED
                                                            |
                                                            v
                     8x NO/NC solder jumper --> 8x Switchcraft RN111PC 1/4" mono jack (tip = NO or NC, sleeve = COM)

9-12VDC barrel jack --> polyfuse --> 7805 --> +5V: Teensy VIN, relay coils, ULN2803A COM
Teensy 3.3 V pin --> +3V3: 6N138 output side + RX1 pull-up
```

## Bill of materials

| Ref | Part | Footprint | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| U1 | PJRC Teensy 4.1 | `Octopus:Teensy41_Socketed` | Mounted on 2x24 female headers. Custom symbol/footprint in this folder (`Octopus.kicad_sym`, `Octopus.pretty`); only the pins this design uses are in the symbol |
| U2 | 6N138 | DIP-8 | MIDI IN opto-isolator; output side runs from the Teensy's 3.3 V |
| U3 | ULN2803A | DIP-18 | Octal Darlington sink driver, internal flyback diodes |
| U4 | L7805 (or Recom R-78E5.0-1.0, see cautions) | TO-220 vertical | 5 V regulator |
| K1-K8 | Omron G5V-1 (5 VDC coil) | `Relay_SPDT_Omron_G5V-1` | SPDT: COM = pins 5+6, NC = pin 1, NO = pin 10 |
| D1 | 1N4148 | DO-35 | Reverse-parallel across the opto LED (MIDI reverse-voltage protection) |
| R1 | 220 Ω | axial 0207 | In series between DIN pin 4 and the opto LED (MIDI spec) |
| R2 | 470 Ω | axial 0207 | Opto output pull-up to **3.3 V** (Teensy 4.1 pins are not 5 V tolerant) |
| R101-R108 | 1 kΩ | axial 0207 | LED series resistor, one per channel |
| LED1-LED8 | 3 mm LED | LED_D3.0mm | Wired in parallel with each relay coil; lights when that relay is energized |
| J1 | JST-XH 5-pin (B5B-XH-A) | JST_XH_B5B-XH-A | Harness to a **panel-mount** 5-pin DIN socket: header pin *n* = DIN pin *n* (only 4 and 5 are used) |
| J2 | 2.1 mm DC barrel jack | BarrelJack_Horizontal | 9-12 VDC in, center positive |
| J3-J10 | Switchcraft RN111PC | `Octopus:Jack_6.35mm_Switchcraft_RN111PC_Vertical` | Channel 1-8 outputs, ¼" 2-conductor, insulated bushing, PC terminals. Sleeve = relay COM; tip = relay NO or NC, chosen by JPn |
| JP1-JP8 | 3-pad solder jumper (PCB copper, not a part) | `SolderJumper-3_P1.3mm_Bridged12` | Per-channel NO/NC select, on the **bottom** side under each jack. Ships bridged to **NO**: the plug is shorted tip-to-sleeve while the channel is on. For **NC** (the plug opens while the channel is on), cut the thin trace between the "NO" pad and the center pad, then solder-bridge the center pad to the "NC" pad |
| F1 | Bourns MF-RHT070 (0.7 A hold) | radial | Input polyfuse |
| H1-H4 | M3 mounting holes | 3.2 mm | Corners |

## Pin map (Teensy 4.1)

| Teensy pin | Function |
|---|---|
| 0 (RX1) | MIDI IN (Serial1), from the opto output |
| 2-9 | Relay 1-8 driver (pin 2 = relay 1 ... pin 9 = relay 8) |
| VIN | +5 V from U4 |
| 3.3V | Powers the 6N138 output side and the RX1 pull-up |
| GND | Common ground |
| USB | Config/debug console (see `firmware/README.md`) |

The firmware's pin table (`firmware/src/RelayBank.cpp`) uses this same map. On the PCB, relay *k* is driven through ULN2803A input I(9−k)/output O(9−k). That reversal only exists so the 16 driver traces between the Teensy and the ULN2803A run straight. It's invisible to the firmware.

## MIDI control spec

- **Program Change (0-127)** recalls a stored preset: all 8 relays are set at once from that preset's 8-bit pattern (bit N = relay N+1, 1 = energized). This is the primary "switch 8 things together" behavior.
- **Control Change**, one CC number per relay (default CC 20-27 for relays 1-8), toggles that single relay live: value >= 64 = on, < 64 = off.
- **MIDI channel**: omni by default; can be pinned to a single channel via the serial config protocol (see firmware README).
- Presets and channel persist across power cycles in the Teensy's emulated EEPROM.

## PCB

- 160 x 100 mm, 2 layers, all through-hole. GND pour on both layers.
- Layout: the Teensy sits top-left with USB at the left edge. The MIDI header, regulator and barrel jack are along the top edge. The ULN2803A sits directly under the Teensy's driver pins. Below that are eight identical channel columns (resistor, LED, relay), and a row of eight RN111PC jacks on 18.5 mm centres along the bottom.
- Net classes (in `Octopus.kicad_pro`): Default 0.3 mm, **Power** (+5V, GND, raw DC in) 0.8 mm, **Relay** (the `/CHn_COM|NO|NC|TIP` contact nets) 1.0 mm. Relay clearance is 0.24 mm because the solder jumper's pads are 0.25 mm apart by design. That's fine for the low-voltage duty these relays are limited to anyway (see cautions). Freerouting routes with a 10 µm margin over every clearance, so its rounding can't land a track under KiCad's rule.
- Verified: `kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity` → 0 errors, 0 unconnected, 0 parity issues. The only warnings are 5 silkscreen-near-edge ones (reference labels by the top edge, and the barrel jack, which overhangs the edge on purpose).

### The RN111PC jacks mount through a panel, not on the board edge

The RN111PC is a Switchcraft Series 11 enclosed jack with PC terminals. Per the Switchcraft catalog (EDG41, p. 100), it stands **perpendicular** to the board: the terminals come out the back of the jack, and the plug tip passes through a 0.25" clearance hole in the PCB (included in the footprint). So:

- The PCB mounts **parallel to, and behind, the panel** the jacks go through. The panel is held by the jacks' 3/8" bushing nuts, and the four M3 holes give extra support. Every other part on the top side (Teensy on headers, relays, TO-220 plus any heatsink) has to be shorter than the jacks' stand-off. Check the jack body height against your parts before fixing the panel spacing.
- The barrel jack and the MIDI harness header point along the board, so they come out through a side wall of the enclosure, not through the jack panel. Say so if you'd rather have them on the same panel.
- Keep the **insulated-bushing** (N/RN) version. On a metal panel, a plain metal-bushing Series 11 would short every channel's sleeve (COM) to chassis and to each other.
- The footprint is drawn from the catalog's recommended layout (tip at −0.250"/+0.022", sleeve at +0.182"/+0.182" from the plug axis), with 2.2 mm round holes to clear the 0.078" × 0.016" blade terminals. I treated "RN111PC" as the RoHS version of the catalog's N111PC. **Check one physical jack against the footprint before ordering boards.**

### Cautions before ordering

1. **Regulator heat.** Worst-case 5 V load is about 370 mA (8 coils × 30 mA, Teensy, LEDs). A 7805 fed from 12 V dissipates about 2.6 W, which is too hot for a bare TO-220. Either fit a heatsink (the tab faces the top edge to leave room) or use a **Recom R-78E5.0-1.0**. It's a pin-compatible switching drop-in that runs cool.
2. **Teensy VIN/VUSB.** If USB may be plugged in while the barrel jack is powered, cut the VIN–VUSB trace on the Teensy's underside (per PJRC). Otherwise the two supplies back-feed each other.
3. **Contact ratings.** The G5V-1 is rated 1 A at 30 VDC (0.5 A at 125 VAC), and the board's clearances are sized for low voltage. **Don't switch mains** with this board as-is.
4. **LED visibility.** The status LEDs are on the board. To see them through an enclosure, use long leads or wire panel LEDs in their place.

## Regenerating

The schematic and board are generated, not hand-drawn:

- `tools/gen_schematic.py` writes `Octopus.kicad_sch` (+ `Octopus.kicad_sym`, `sym-lib-table`). Symbol UUIDs are derived from reference designators, so PCB links survive regeneration.
- `tools/gen_teensy_fp.py` and `tools/gen_jack_fp.py` write the Teensy 4.1 and RN111PC footprints into `Octopus.pretty/`.
- `tools/gen_pcb.py` exports the netlist, places footprints, autoroutes, pours GND and saves `Octopus.kicad_pcb`. It must run with KiCad's bundled Python (`"C:/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/python.exe" tools/gen_pcb.py`). Routing needs [Freerouting](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting) 2.4.1 and a Java 25 runtime; the paths are set at the top of the script, or via `FREEROUTING_JAR` / `JAVA25`. Pass `--no-route` for placement only.

Re-running any of these **overwrites** its output. Once you start editing the schematic or layout by hand in KiCad, stop using the scripts (or port your edits into them first). Intermediate files land in `build/`, which is git-ignored.
